facts.value: Caodaism is a melting pot of many of the world’s largest faiths, originating in 1921. It teaches harmony, unity with a monotheistic deity, reincarnation, and anti-materialism.
Belief in several creator spirits and devils, similar to Abrahamic faiths.
Caodaism was influential in Vietnam during the 1930s, especially for its anti-colonialist sentiment against the French occupation.
In 1997, the practice of Caodaism was permitted again in Vietnam after being banned for 22 years.
Students of the faiths spend years honing their self-control and ability to grow through introspection.
Scholars of each belief often borrow from each other, exemplified by C.S. Lewis integrating the concept of Tao into his writings.
